caption: One half of Gummi Bears, a PWF tag team billed on the fed's own dedicated bio card (promotions/pwf-powersite/archive/bio-gummi-bears.html).

name: Jason "The Goat" Doods
caption: Won a Trio Ladder Match at THE PWF REBIRTH to become the fed's new and undisputed World Champion, opening 2000's relaunch as its own new top star.

tenures.note: Won a fatal-elimination gauntlet (First Blood over "Bad Boy" Marcus T.) to reach, then won, the Trio Ladder Match for the PWF World Title against Soniq and Inferno at THE PWF REBIRTH, 1 October 2000 — the fed's own relaunch broadcast. Attacked and stripped of the physical belt after the show by Marcus T., who vowed a rematch; no further appearance survives in this capture.

name: "Bad Boy" Marcus T.
caption: Lost a First Blood match to Jason Doods at THE PWF REBIRTH, then attacked the new champion after the bell and made off with the belt.

tenures.note: Lost a First Blood Match to Jason Doods after referee Rick Strict ruled him bled first; attacked Strict post-match with the Run N Gun. After Doods won the World Title later the same night, Marcus T. jumped him backstage, took the belt, tossed it back to Doods, and vowed "NEXT TIME, THIS BELT GOES AROUND MY WAIST."

identity.note: A shared "Marcus T" nickname with an unrelated WWA wrestler (full ring name "Marcus Dark Heart T"); no corroborating link to this PWF character.

name: Toby DiRizzo
caption: Beat Ambrose Fleetwood in a Hardcore Match at THE PWF REBIRTH before losing to Soniq in the semifinal round.

tenures.note: Made Ambrose Fleetwood submit to the Screw the System in 26 seconds to reach the semifinals, then lost to Soniq (chair-assisted) in the semifinal round of THE PWF REBIRTH's World Title tournament.

identity.note: A decorated-nickname collision ("The Authority") with an unrelated character billed "Beat Down Authority"; no corroborating link to this PWF character.

name: Ambrose Fleetwood
caption: Lost a Hardcore Match to Toby DiRizzo by submission in the opening round of THE PWF REBIRTH's World Title tournament.

tenures.note: Billed as disdainful of DiRizzo's manners; submitted to the Screw the System in 26 seconds.

identity.note: A decorated-nickname collision ("The Golden Child") with an unrelated RSPWF wrestler; no corroborating link to this PWF character.

name: Soniq
caption: Advanced to THE PWF REBIRTH's own three-way World Title final by beating Dark Cloak and Toby DiRizzo, then lost the title match after vanishing mid-match, dragged out by Dark Cloak.

tenures.note: Billed "Alecs Johnson" in the ring-action text (his finisher is named the "SoniqDown"). Beat a mysterious stalker, Dark Cloak, by sleeperhold when the lights came back on; beat Toby DiRizzo with a stolen chair to reach the World Title final; was dragged out of the ring and vanished during the Trio Ladder Match, finishing the tournament without a fall against him.

name: Dark Cloak
caption: A mysterious figure who stalked Soniq through a PWF POWERHOUR angle before losing to him at THE PWF REBIRTH, then dragged Soniq out of the ring during the World Title final.

tenures.note: Introduced in a flashback as a hooded stalker who ambushed Soniq on television and left him with an "M Flag"; lost the resulting match when the arena lights cut out and Soniq was left alone in his own sleeperhold. Resurfaced during the Trio Ladder World Title match to drag Soniq from the ring.

identity.note: A decorated-name collision with an unrelated character elsewhere in the registry billed bare "Cloak"; no corroborating link to this PWF character.

name: Havoc
caption: Billed as a former PWF World Champion returning from a mystery attacker's ambush; lost to the newly revealed Inferno at THE PWF REBIRTH.

identity.note: A near-identical name (Havoc vs. Havok) within this same wing, but confirmed distinct people: this Havoc is billed "the former PWF champion" returning from hiatus in the October 2000 REBIRTH broadcast, while havok-pwf's own dedicated 2001 bio card states outright "He has not been in any federation at this point" — the two cards directly contradict a shared identity. Also a bare-name collision with unrelated Havoc/Havok characters in other unrelated promotions elsewhere in the registry (euwc, cswa, faw, iwf, wwa) — no corroborating link to any of them either.

tenures.note: Billed "the former PWF champion," returning to a celebration interrupted by an unidentified attacker for several weeks; lost the rematch when the attacker was revealed as Inferno, taken out by the Carnage Crush.

name: Inferno
caption: Unmasked as Havoc's mystery attacker at THE PWF REBIRTH, then fought through the semifinals before losing the World Title final to Jason Doods.

tenures.note: Billed "from Parts Unknown"; revealed as Havoc's mystery attacker and beat him with the Carnage Crush. Beat Chris Cabana (with an assist from Havoc taking out the Miller Brothers) to reach the World Title final, then was knocked off a ladder by a thrown ladder from Havoc and lost the title to Jason Doods.

identity.note: A generic ring name shared with unrelated characters elsewhere in the registry; no corroborating link to this PWF wrestler, billed "the Unknown-Unnamed Being" and revealed as Inferno at THE PWF REBIRTH.

name: Skanker
caption: Lost a Hell in a Cell match to Chris Cabana at THE PWF REBIRTH after allying with two visiting WWA wrestlers who turned on him.

tenures.note: Challenged Chris Cabana to a Hell in a Cell match after Cabana flirted with his girlfriend, Two-Tone. Two visiting WWA wrestlers (billed "the Miller Brothers") climbed the cage as his apparent allies but sided with Cabana instead, and Cabana escaped the cage with them for the win.

identity.note: A near-name collision with an unrelated GLW character billed "Skank"; no corroborating link to this PWF character.

name: Chris Cabana
caption: Won a Hell in a Cell match over Skanker with an assist from two visiting WWA wrestlers, then fell to Inferno in the World Title tournament's semifinal round.

tenures.note: Won a Hell in a Cell match over Skanker (executing the Poolside Plunge) with the surprise help of two visiting WWA wrestlers, billed "the Miller Brothers." Lost the semifinal round to Inferno after Skanker returned the favor with a chair shot of his own.

identity.note: A generic-first-name collision with an unrelated EWA manager and with this same wing's own Christopher Chaos; no corroborating link — Chris Cabana and Christopher Chaos are two distinct PWF wrestlers who never share a scene in this capture.

name: Two-Tone
caption: Skanker's girlfriend, billed ringside for his Hell in a Cell match at THE PWF REBIRTH.

tenures.note: Named as Skanker's girlfriend, the object of Chris Cabana's flirting that started their feud; shown ringside worried during the Hell in a Cell match.

name: Wolfgang Rainier G.
caption: A returning former PWF Tag-Team Champion whose mystery-match draw with the Hatawman was cut short when Jason Doods laid both men out with a lead pipe.

tenures.note: Billed as "the former PWF Tag-Team Title holder" returning after a two-year absence (an undated prior reign, not sequenced in the reign ledger). Ruled a draw with The Hatawman when Jason Doods ran in and knocked both men out with a lead pipe.

name: The Hatawman
caption: A returning PWF veteran whose mystery-match draw with Wolfgang Rainier G. was cut short by a Jason Doods run-in.

tenures.note: Billed as a returning veteran wrestling "two years" of ring rust off; hit the Hatawkick on Wolfgang Rainier G. before Jason Doods ran in and laid both men out with a lead pipe, ruled a draw.

name: Ace Cooper
caption: Won a PWF Tag-team #1 contendership for T3 at THE PWF REBIRTH with a chain-assisted pin, courtesy of Big Mama Sledge.

tenures.note: The only member of the stable T3 named directly performing in the ring; caught Moon Glorious with chains thrown in by Big Mama Sledge and hit the BC Drop for the win.

name: Big Mama Sledge
caption: T3's own ringside enforcer, whose chain toss to Ace Cooper decided T3's PWF Tag-team #1 contendership match at THE PWF REBIRTH.

tenures.note: Ringside with T3; threw Ace Cooper a set of chains that decided the match. Backstage afterward, T3 was seen "draped with the M flag" alongside her, an off-screen attack implied by sound alone.

identity.note: A decorated-name collision with an unrelated character elsewhere in the registry billed bare "Sledge"; no corroborating link to this PWF manager.

name: Moon Glorious
caption: Half of the Hardcore Machines, pinned by a chain-assisted Ace Cooper at THE PWF REBIRTH.

tenures.note: Named inconsistently across the broadcast's own text as "Moon," "the Moon Man," and "Moon Glorious" — read here as one wrestler. Pinned after Ace Cooper's chain-assisted BC Drop.

name: Napalm
caption: Half of the Hardcore Machines, on the losing end of T3's PWF Tag-team #1 contendership win at THE PWF REBIRTH.

tenures.note: Tagged with Moon Glorious as the Hardcore Machines; lost the #1 contendership match when Big Mama Sledge's interference turned the match T3's way.

name: Commissioner Zoe
caption: The PWF's newly appointed on-air commissioner, credited in THE PWF REBIRTH's own flashback footage with setting up the broadcast's mystery match.

tenures.note: Named only in a PWF POWERHOUR-set flashback replayed inside THE PWF REBIRTH's own broadcast, announcing a "special secret match" between "two returning Powerstars" — the mystery match resolved in-show as Wolfgang Rainier G. vs. The Hatawman. Never shown in the broadcast's own present-tense action.

name: Destroyer
caption: One half of the Ruff Ryders (with Devastator), whose tag team debut win over the Lords of Destruction opened the PWF's own 2001 relaunch television taping.

Helped Devastator beat the Lords of Destruction (Bloodstorm & Carnage) at Saturday Night Havoc, then joined Devastator in attacking the debuting Waveriders and Gods of War before their own scheduled match could start.

identity.note: A generic ring name shared with unrelated characters elsewhere in the registry; no corroborating link to this PWF Ruff Ryders tag wrestler.

name: T-Bomb
caption: One half of the debuting Waveriders tag team, attacked by the Ruff Ryders before his own PWF debut match could begin.

tenures.note: No dedicated bio card survives. Billed at a combined 410 lbs with tag partner Riptide; the Waveriders' scheduled match against the Gods of War never started — the Ruff Ryders attacked both teams on the way to the ring.

name: Dave Harley
caption: Color commentator, on-air for his own first PWF broadcast alongside Jason Stanyer at the fed's 2001 relaunch television taping.

tenures.note: Billed "the 'Big Dawg'"; his own on-air line, welcomed to "my first event," places this as his debut broadcast.

identity.note: A bare name/nickname collision with unrelated wrestlers/commentators elsewhere in the registry; no corroborating link to this PWF commentator.

name: Johnny Mayhem
caption: A backstage interviewer, punched through the windshield of Bloodbath's own car during a parking-lot interview at Saturday Night Havoc.

tenures.note: Interviewed Bloodbath about his new Dodge Durango and softer gimmick; Bloodbath took offense, punched him down, and delivered the Bloodbash through his own car's windshield.
